comparison.objective: Candidate tunes and locks a robot-axis damper for safe dynamic stopping; pr-1800 seats a sleeve while registering a radial oil passage.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires hex-key engagement, counterholding, collar rotation, torque-limited relocking, and iterative impact testing. pr-1800 requires grasp-preserved angular registration and clearance-fit insertion/release.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two acceptable physical stopping cycles at ≥0.85 J, within 12 mm stroke, followed by lock-retention testing. pr-1800 requires released seating within pose tolerances and an unobstructed 10 mm passage for 1 s.
comparison.reason: The tested abilities differ meaningfully: dynamic damping adjustment and retained locking versus free-part insertion with port registration. Shared fine alignment is only generic. Candidate rubric still lacks numeric definitions for excessive rebound, overload, and the declared collar-drift tolerance.
